title: Rising Support for Political Violence Is Associated With Perceived Political Discrimination
abstract: Abstract: Election periods can heighten political conflict and support for political violence. Using two-wave panel data from the East German state elections study 2024 (EGSES24) in Saxony, Thuringia, and Brandenburg ( N = 1,053), we examined how support for political violence changed from before to after the elections and whether this change was linked to perceived electoral loss and perceived political discrimination. Support for political violence increased slightly after the elections. This increase was associated with increases in perceived political discrimination, particularly among individuals high in social dominance orientation. Perceived electoral success did not explain the increase in political violence endorsement. These findings suggest that experiences of political discrimination, rather than electoral defeat as such, may help explain rising support for political violence during election periods.
